_comment: Hand-written sample explanations shown in DEMO mode (no API key). Real, accurate, beginner-facing. Keyed by lowercased card name. These let you preview the finished look before connecting a paid API key.

lightning bolt.in_plain_words: A cheap, fast spell that deals 3 damage to anything you choose — a creature, a player, or a planeswalker.
lightning bolt.when_you_can_play_it: It's an instant, so you can play it almost any time, even during your opponent's turn or in the middle of combat — as long as you have one red mana.
how_it_works: Choose any target: a creature, a player, or a planeswalker.
It deals 3 damage to that target.
A creature with 3 or less toughness is destroyed; a player loses 3 life.

words_to_know.definition: A spell you can cast at almost any time, including on other players' turns.
One red mana, paid from a red source such as a Mountain.
Lowers a creature's toughness for the turn (enough destroys it) or reduces a player's life total.
You choose what it hits: a creature, a player, or a planeswalker.

lightning bolt.example_turn: Your opponent attacks with a 3/3 creature. Before damage happens, you cast Lightning Bolt targeting it, dealing 3 damage — the creature is destroyed and never hits you.

llanowar elves.in_plain_words: A small green creature whose job is to make extra mana. Tap it to get one green mana to help cast your other spells.
llanowar elves.when_you_can_play_it: Play it like any creature — on your own turn, during your main phase, when nothing else is happening.
how_it_works: Pay {G} to put the 1/1 Elf onto the battlefield.
It has "summoning sickness" the turn it arrives, so you can't tap it for mana until your next turn (unless something gives it haste).
After that, tap it ({T}) to add one green mana to spend on spells or abilities.
You can do this once per turn; it untaps at the start of your next turn.

words_to_know.definition: Turn the creature sideways to use its ability; it can't be used again until it untaps.
Produce one green mana.
The resource you spend to cast spells and use abilities.
A creature can't attack or use {T} abilities until you've controlled it since the start of your turn.

llanowar elves.example_turn: Turn 1 you play a Forest and cast Llanowar Elves. Turn 2 you play another Forest and tap the Elf — now you have 3 mana available instead of 2, letting you cast something bigger a turn early.

serra angel.in_plain_words: A strong 4/4 flying creature that can attack and still stay back to defend on the same turn.
serra angel.when_you_can_play_it: On your own turn, during your main phase, when you have five mana including two white.
how_it_works: Pay {3}{W}{W} to put the 4/4 Angel onto the battlefield.
Because it has flying, only creatures with flying or reach can block it.
Because it has vigilance, attacking with it doesn't tap it — so it's still available to block on your opponent's next turn.

words_to_know.definition: Can only be blocked by creatures with flying or reach.
Attacking doesn't tap this creature, so it can still block afterward.
Three mana of any color plus two white mana.
Power 4 (the damage it deals) and toughness 4 (the damage needed to destroy it).

serra angel.example_turn: You attack with Serra Angel in the air for 4 damage. Normally attacking taps a creature, but vigilance keeps it untapped — so when your opponent swings back, the Angel is still ready to block.

counterspell.in_plain_words: A reactive spell that stops an opponent's spell from happening at all.
counterspell.when_you_can_play_it: It's an instant, so you hold it and cast it in response to a spell your opponent is casting — before that spell takes effect.
how_it_works: Wait until an opponent casts a spell.
In response, cast Counterspell, paying {U}{U}, and target that spell.
The targeted spell is "countered": it does nothing and goes to its owner's graveyard without ever happening.

words_to_know.definition: Stop a spell so it never takes effect; it goes to the graveyard instead.
Castable any time, including during an opponent's turn.
Two blue mana.
You must point it at a specific spell that is currently being cast.

counterspell.example_turn: Your opponent casts a big creature. While that spell is still waiting to resolve, you cast Counterspell targeting it — the creature is countered and never enters play.

giant growth.in_plain_words: A cheap combat trick that makes one creature much bigger for the rest of the turn.
giant growth.when_you_can_play_it: It's an instant, so you can cast it any time — most often during combat to surprise your opponent.
how_it_works: Pay {G} and choose a target creature (yours or an opponent's).
That creature gets +3/+3 — its power and toughness each go up by 3.
The bonus lasts until the end of the turn, then wears off.

words_to_know.definition: Castable any time, including during combat.
Adds 3 to power and 3 to toughness.
The effect disappears when the turn ends.
An instant played during combat to win a fight or push extra damage.

giant growth.example_turn: Your 2/2 is blocked by a 3/3. Before combat damage, you cast Giant Growth on your creature, making it 5/5 — it survives and destroys the 3/3 instead of dying.
